newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower, spot September expires.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower, spot September expires.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices ended mainly lower Wednesday, with the nearby months taking the brunt of the day's losses, after a steady bout of commission house selling, trading sources said.

The spot September contract, which went off the board today, slid 3.00 cents a lb, to finish at 109.20 cents. September's premium to second-position December continued to shrink, falling to 4.80 cents, compared to 6.35 cents at the close Tuesday.

Benchmark December futures ended 1.45 cents lower, at 104.40, after trading between 107.00 and 104.00. December's premium to the March 1997 contract also narrowed, ending at 3.45 cents versus 3.95 cents Tuesday.

Concerns about low consumer stock levels in the U.S, which have long supported steep nearby premiums, were fading, traders said, as new-crop coffees from Central and South America are expected to replenish warehouse stocks during the coming months.

Traders also noted the U.S. Commerce Department's report released Wednesday, which showed unroasted coffee imports rose to 79,713 tonnes in July, compared to 74,144 tonnes in June and 67,002 tonnes in July 1995.
"If the U.S is able to import coffee, it may have alleviated supply concerns," one trader said.
Technically, traders said December's close below 105 cents was bearish and may signal a test of the closely watched 100-cent mark is looming.
Volume on the day was moderate, at an estimated 7,069 lots.
